STAFF COMMENTS:

City Manager de Geus reported that the Malibu/Lost Hills Sheriffs Station held a Safety
Symposium on November 19, 2022 at the Westlake Village Civic Center. Speakers and
vendors covered many topics for the attendees.

A Paper Shredding Day event was held on December 3, 2022 at the Westlake Civic
Center. The event was coordinated by Waste Management and Shred My Files. The
City's next Shredding Day event will be in Spring 2023.

Holidays in the Village and the Holiday Sing-Along event was held on December 4, 2022
and was well attended despite the rainy weather. City staff manned a City booth and City
Council participated in the Sing-Along.

COUNCIL COMMENTS:

Councilmember Honig thanked the Westlake Village Rotary Clubs for their support and
participation in the Holidays in the Village event, allowing the Rotary Clubs to raise funds
to give back to the community.

CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

1.  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMITTEE REPORT:

  City Manager de Geus reported that the Public Safety Committee (Halpern/Davis)
  met on November 2, 2022 and that staff will be presenting reports on two of the
  topics discussed at that meeting.
   City Council Minutes
  City of Westlake Village  December 14, 2022  3

  CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE REPORTS (continued):

l  Reckless Driving Reporting Program
  Deputy City Manager Eskandar reported on the Sheriff's Teen Traffic Offender
  Program (STTOP) which was developed in the early 2000's to help curb dangerous
  driving behavior by teenagers. The theory behind the program was that the
  presence of a uniformed Deputy showing up to have a conversation with an
  individual and their parents would be a strong deterrent and that dangerous
  behavior would be corrected. The program ended in 2015.

  The Pedestrian Safety Study, adopted by the City Council on January 12, 2022,
  recommended launching a program, building on the previous successes of
  STTOP, and aimed to prevent reckless driving.

  The new pilot program, Reckless Driving Reporting Program (RDRP), will function
  to reach drivers of all ages. This program starts with reporting the reckless driving
  through the City's website. The observations provided through the City's website
  will not directly result in a citation being issued as the violation must be observed
  by a Deputy for a citation. However, the Deputy will review the data submitted and
  send a letter to the registered owner of the vehicle. As a pilot program, staff will
  monitor the impact on law enforcement. Reckless driving emergencies should
  continue to be reported to 911 immediately.

  The Public Safety Committee supported the launch of the RDRP. Additionally, the
  RDRP was presented to and supported by the City's Public Safety Advisory Board
  at their November 14, 2022 meeting. Mr. Eskandar stated that if the City Council
  is supportive, staff will proceed with launching and advertising the RDRP at the
  start of 2023 through the various communications channels typically used such as
  the City's mailed newsletter, video newsletter, and social media.

  No motion was required for the pilot Reckless Driving Reporting Program. Staff
  will report back to City Council on the progress of the program.

  Volunteers on Patrol Vehicle
  Administrative Analyst Mott introduced the item addressing the need to replace the

j  current 2009 Ford Escape Volunteers on Patrol vehicle as the cost of repairs
  exceeds the value of the vehicle. In 2019, staff applied for and was awarded a
  $70,000 grant from the Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy for the purchase of
  a new Volunteers on Patrol vehicle that will also serve as an Arson/Fire Watch
  Patrol vehicle. This grant is expected to cover the purchase cost of a new vehicle
  as well as the outfitting of the vehicle with lights, sirens, and technology estimated
  at an additional $14,000-$16,000 for equipment and labor.

  Staff presented two vehicle options for City Council consideration: Ford Explorer
  XLT, a standard patrol vehicle for the Sheriff's Department at the cost of $38,760,
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  December 14. 2022  4

CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE REPORTS (continued):

  or an all-electric Ford Mustang Mach-E, starting at $46,895, used by other law
  enforcement jurisdictions.

  The Public Safety Committee recommended the purchase of a Mustang Mach-E
  due to the sustainable nature of the vehicle and the potential for reduced operating
  costs.

  Councilmember Halpern moved to authorize the City Manager to purchase a new
  Volunteers on Patrol Vehicle, the Ford Mustang Mach-E, and submit for
  reimbursement from the grant awarded by the Santa Monica Mountains
  Conservancy. Councilmember Mcsweeney seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Halpern, Mcsweeney, Honig, Mayor Pro
  Tern Davis, and Mayor Pearl.

2.  CULTURAL RECREATION COMMITTEE REPORT:

  City Manager de Geus reported that the Cultural Recreation Committee met on
  October 25. 2022 (Councilmember Honig; Councilmember Mcsweeney was
  unable to attend). City Clerk Mann reported on two Veteran items discussed at
  the meeting.

  America Supporting Americans
  On July 22, 2022 City Council moved to have the Cultural Recreation Committee
  review America Supporting Americans (ASA) and consider supporting them. While
  preparing for the October 25 meeting, staff discovered that City Council adopted
  Resolution 1914-17 which supports ASA. The Cultural Recreation Committee
  reconfirmed the City support for ASA and requested that staff work more
  proactively with ASA to continue the support.

  No motion was required for the current support for America Supporting Americans
  as stated in Resolution 1914-17.

  Veterans Memorial Project
  City Clerk Mann reported the Fiscal Year 2022-23 budget includes $25,000 for the
  Veterans Memorial project and reviewed the Art in Public Places policy. A Veterans
  Memorial project approach was then presented along with the request for direction
  from the City Council to develop a solicitation package.
   City Council Minutes
  City of Westlake Village  December 14, 2022  5

  CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE REPORTS (continued):

l  City Manager de Geus presented the budget and future design and construction
  funding need with the recommendation to utilize the Civic Center Fountain
  refurbishment funds for the Veterans Memorial project.

  City Engineer Hughes presented solicitation package topics and City Clerk Mann
  presented the next steps for the project.

  Council discussion included the location of the fountains at the Civic Center and
  possibly selecting one fountain to be re-purposed for a Veterans Memorial, Council
  recommended the target to complete the project be more realistic post 2023;
  discussion also included budget and developing a comprehensive plan for the
  removal of all water features to create a more inviting City Civic Center courtyard
  as the City considers a Veterans Memorial project.

  Staff received City Council direction and noted that a revised project approach will
  be taken back to the Cultural Recreation Committee for review and input.

  Administrative Services Director Wilson reviewed the Fiscal Year (FY) 2021-22
  adopted budget stating that staff has reconciled all revenue and expenditures as
  of June 30, 2022. Revenues received ($15,693,163) exceeded the budget amount
  ($12,222,818), by an additional $3.47 million in revenue primarily due to increased
  Transient Occupancy, Property and Sales Tax receipts. Expenditures budgeted,
  as amended ($13,279,695) were higher than actual expenditures ($10,841,250),
  resulting in expenditures coming in under budget by $2.438 million.

  A review of the first quarter of FY 2022-23 indicates continuing strong performance
  in Sales Tax, Property Tax and Transient Occupancy Tax. Some revenues are
  anticipated to exceed adopted estimates while expenditures are projected to be
  within budget.

  Administrative Services Director Wilson advised that a mid-year review will be

  2.  INTRODUCTION OF ORDINANCE 299-23 - ELECTRONIC CAMPAIGN
  DISCLOSURE STATEMENT FILING:

  City Clerk Mann presented Ordinance 299-23, which will allow for automated
  compliance with Assembly Bill 2151, which mandates the City Clerk to post within
  72 hours of receipt, all campaign filing on the City website. Posted forms must
  comply with Fair Political Practices Commission (FPPC) regulations, which
  included fields that must be redacted for public viewing.

  Government Code Section 84615 states that the City Council must adopt an
  ordinance before Campaign Electronic Filing systems are utilized and the software
  must be secure, not create unduly burden to the filers, confirm filing with a
  timestamp and ensure the integrity of the data.

  City Clerk Mann stated a Public Portal link will be added to the website for 24/7
  searching. A backfile conversion project will be conducted as FPPC states that
  all elected officials campaign filings have a permanent retention, allowing for all
  previously filed forms to be in a single database.

  City Clerk Mann is currently working with the vendor to set up the software, which
  includes FPPC testing. Software will he used for the 2024 Election and City Council
  will also be able to use it for annual Form 470's filings.

j  Councilmember Honig moved to be introduced by title only and that further reading
  be waived for Ordinance No. 299-23, titled 'An Ordinance of the City of Westlake
  Village Regarding Electronic Campaign Disclosure Statement Filing and

  exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act. Councilmember Halpern
